contents.name: Theorem 2 (Alexander's theorem): every knot or link in S^3 is represented by a closed braid
Theorem 3 (Reidemeister's theorem): two diagrams of the same link differ by planar isotopy and the three Reidemeister moves
Theorem 4 (Markov's theorem): closed braid representatives of the same link are related by Markov moves
Lemma 2.1: a reducing move transforms D into D' with h(D') = h(D) - 1
Corollary 2.2: any sequence of reducing moves has length at most h(D)
Lemma 2.2: if h(D) > 0 the Seifert picture contains a defect region
Corollary 2.1 (Yamada): the minimum number of Seifert circles equals the braid index
contents.reason: This equality is not consumed by any scaffolded item of the pair: the braid-index definition uses only Alexander existence, and adding the extremal theorem would be new scope beyond the commissioned Markov route.

Figure 10: the case where two reducing arcs at a peak intersect once
Lemma 2.7: classification of irreducible peaks into c-pairs and d-pairs
Lemma 2.8 and its sketch: an irreducible peak of height n+1 is replaced by Markov sequences; at most four bands occur

Lemma 2.6: the base case of the peak induction (no peaks below the ambient height)
Sections 1.1-1.2: geometric braids, their product and the Artin presentation
Section 1.3: the configuration-space model of the braid group
Section 4.2: the Markov trace on the Hecke tower and the Burau/Alexander determinant formula
contents.reason: The Hecke-trace, HOMFLYPT and Burau determinant material is the commissioned content of the later BG-12 pair, which the plan already places after this one; no item of the present pair consumes it.

sources.title: Traczyk, A new proof of Markov's braid theorem, Banach Center Publications 42 (1998), 409-419
sources.locator: Complete article, printed pp. 409-419: Theorem 1, Theorem 2, Proposition 3, Lemma 4 with its corollary, Lemma 5, and Figures 1-11.

contents.name: Theorem 1 (Markov 1935): closed braids of the same oriented link are related by braid isotopies and Markov moves
Theorem 2: the length of any reducing sequence taking D to a closed braid is exactly h(D)
Proposition 3: smoothing crossings does not increase the number of defect areas
contents.reason: This observation supports Traczyk's own route to the disjoint-arc reduction; the scaffolded peak-reduction item instead follows the survey's Lemma 2.4 argument, so the observation is not consumed anywhere in this pair.

sources.locator: Sections 1-3, PDF pp. 1-11: Theorem 1, Theorem 2, Sections 3.1-3.2 (diagrams and isotopies), Sections 3.3-3.6 (the three conditions and completeness), Figures 2, 4, 5 and 6.

contents.name: Theorem 1 (Reidemeister's theorem)
Theorem 2 (multijet transversality theorem)
Section 3.1: the three conditions defining a knot diagram (immersion, transverse double points, no higher multiplicity)
Section 3.3 and Figure 6: the first condition (vertical tangencies) yields the first Reidemeister move
Section 3.4: the second condition (transverse triple points) yields the third Reidemeister move
Section 3.5: the third condition (a double point with collinear projected derivatives) yields the second Reidemeister move

contents.reason: These extensions concern other diagram theories with their own invariants; nothing in the oriented-link, Markov-equivalence or braid-closure route scaffolded here depends on them.
